tone_statements.citation: Lacroix, Pierre-Francis. 1971. [Compte rendu de] Hermann Jungraithmayr, Die Ron-Sprachen. Tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien (Afrikanistische Forschungen III), Glückstadt: J. J. Augustin, 1970 [joint notice with Johannes Lukas, Studien zur Sprache der Gisiga]. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 41(2): 273-274.
tone_statements.quote: Pour chacune de ces langues le Dr Jungraithmayr présente une étude morphologique très complète, suivie d'un texte et d'un vocabulaire à deux entrées comportant 170 unités. Le lecteur en aurait donc une étude exhaustive s'il avait aussi à sa disposition les analyses phonologiques et tonologiques correspondantes qui, sauf pour le Fyer, sont absentes de cet ouvrage, et si y figurait également l'examen des questions de syntaxe, tous sujets qui doivent être abordés dans une publication ultérieure.
tone_statements.translation: For each of these languages Dr Jungraithmayr presents a very complete morphological study, followed by a text and a two-way vocabulary of 170 items. The reader would thus have an exhaustive study if he also had at his disposal the corresponding phonological and tonological analyses which, except for Fyer, are absent from this work, and if syntax were also treated - all subjects to be taken up in a later publication.
tone_statements.locator: p. 273 (Comptes rendus), first paragraph of the review

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2003. Why reconstructing Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (Chadic Linguistics 1), 21-42. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: Section 3 Phonology (vowels, consonants, prosodies of labialisation/palatalisation) and 3.3 Tones: 'All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones and this can therefore be posited in Proto-Ron. Tones have significant grammatical functions as well as lexical.' Nothing whatever on stress or accent; Fyer discussed only as the most conservative lect (with Tambas). downloaded from Internet Archive copy 2015-04-21 of rogerblench.info; 75-dpi image scan, scanned with tesseract at a 200-dpi render.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. Dictionary of Lis ma Run (Ron of Bokkos): draft for comment. 93 pp.
sources.note: Bokkos (bokk1249), a sister Ron language, not Fyer; front matter covers parts of speech only; a full-text search for stress/accent gives nothing.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Adedamola Aregbesola, Christina Riepe, Iris Sacson, John Sacson & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rom (Tambas) [tdk] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-018. SIL International. 50 pp.
sources.note: Recent SIL survey of Tambas, Fyer's closest relative, with a wordlist; low chance of a stress statement but it is the only recent field report on the Fyer-Tambas branch. sil.org could not be reached by automated download to the fetcher.
